$schema_note: Per-app rule weightings. One review harness, three different problems -- and the
weighting is where the difference lives, not in three forks of the detector.
A weight multiplies a finding's severity to rank the report. It NEVER changes
whether a rule fires: that is the false-positive budget's territory, and a rule
that needs its weight lowered to be tolerable is a rule that should not have
passed the budget. Weight 0 SUPPRESSES a class from the report body, and the
router prints what it suppressed and why -- a silently dropped class reads as
'nothing found there', which is the one thing a coverage claim may never do.
`gestalt` decides whether the page itself earns a model call for the questions
no rule may claim -- hierarchy, attention, whether the page makes sense. This is
the expensive knob and the one that differs most between these three apps.
Bounds: these weights are editorial judgements about what each app is FOR,
derived from the app inventory in the research README, not measurements. They
order a report; they are not evidence about anything. The severities they
multiply come from the rules, which are measured.

default.label: unweighted
default.why: Every class at parity. The baseline a profile has to justify departing from, and the right choice for an app nobody has characterised yet.

reso-landing-app.label: marketing aesthetics
why: Next 14, purchased template. The design system is someone else's and was
bought deliberately, so linting it for token conformance reports the
purchase rather than a defect -- high volume, all of it correct-by-decision,
and it buries the findings that matter. What matters here is whether the
page persuades: hierarchy, where the eye lands, whether the render betrays
the intent. That is the judgement layer's work, so gestalt runs on every
page and is the point of the run rather than a garnish.
Correctness classes are NOT relaxed. Contrast and target size are legal and
physical facts about a reader, not house style, and a bought template has no
standing to fail them.

reso-management-app.label: design-system conformance
why: Next 16, React 19, Tailwind 4, and the design system is ours. Here the
deterministic layer does nearly all the work, because almost every question
worth asking has a number in the answer: is this the token, is this on the
grid, is this on the scale, is this reachable. Drift is the defect class,
and drift is exactly what a rule catches and a model guesses at.
Gestalt is throttled rather than disabled. An internal operations tool is
judged on whether it is correct and consistent, not on whether it is
beautiful, and a hierarchy call on every screen of a large app is the single
most expensive thing this pipeline can be asked to do for the least return.
A small budget keeps the capability without letting it set the bill.

reso-web-app.label: between the two
why: Next 13, public-facing but built in-house, so both readings apply and
neither dominates. Conformance is checkable because the system is ours;
persuasion matters because a customer sees it. Left near parity
deliberately: an app characterised as 'between' has not been characterised,
and inventing a confident weighting for it would be the kind of plausible
number this bench exists to refuse.
